memos.headline: MSFT and JPM Lead Broad Rally; NVDA Overextended; UNH in Freefall
memos.body: I see a market that has staged a sharp V-shaped recovery over the past four weeks, but the leaders are now stretched. MSFT sits 14.7% above its 50-day mean with an RSI of 76.7 and only 2.8% off its 52-week high—strong relative strength (+10.6% vs SPY over 4w) but overbought and vulnerable to a pullback. NVDA is the most extended name in the universe at +20.2% above its 50-day mean with RSI 72.9 after a blistering +33.4% four-week run; I'd wait for a consolidation toward the 50-day before adding. UNH is a technical disaster—RSI 19.8, down 53.3% from its high, and 37.6% below its 50-day mean—this is a falling knife I have no interest in catching until price stabilizes above 320. AMZN and CAT offer the best risk/reward: both have reclaimed their 200-day means with RSIs in the low 60s-70s and positive 4-week relative strength, though CAT's 26-week return of -15.2% reminds me the longer trend is still damaged.

views.note: Strong trend and relative strength but RSI 76.7 signals overbought; I'd trim above 460 and reverse my view on a close below 420 (roughly the 50-day mean).
Explosive +33.4% 4w rally has pushed price 20% above the 50-day mean with RSI 72.9; prefer to wait for a pullback toward ~115-120 before getting long, and would turn negative below 110.
RSI 61.3 with price above both moving averages and positive 4w relative strength vs SPY (+6.2%); would exit on a close below 190 which would breach the 200-day mean.
Only 4.4% off its 52-week high, 13.2% above the 200-day mean, RSI 71.8 with positive relative strength on all timeframes; low ATR of 1.92% makes this a quality trend—would reassess below 250.
RSI 19.8, down 53% from highs, 45% below the 200-day mean with ATR 6.69%—this is a broken chart and catching this knife is reckless until price holds above 320 for multiple sessions.
Flat 4w return (+1.2%), below both moving averages, and -11.7% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks; no edge here until it reclaims 112 or breaks below 104.
Barely above the 50-day mean (+1.3%) but still 6.6% below the 200-day with negative 4w and 12w relative strength vs SPY; needs to reclaim 220 to turn constructive.
Strong 4w bounce of +20.2% with positive relative strength, but still 15% off highs and below the 200-day mean; I'd hold with a stop below 320.

memos.headline: GOOGL and MSFT Show Durable Earnings Power; CAT and XOM Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see the clearest fundamental strength in GOOGL and MSFT this quarter. GOOGL posted 12% YoY revenue growth to $90.2B with a remarkable 38.3% net margin and net income up 46% YoY on just $14.8B of total debt—this is the best margin-to-leverage profile in the universe. MSFT delivered 13.3% revenue growth to $70.1B with 36.9% net margins and net income up 17.7% YoY, all on moderate $42.9B debt. On the other end, CAT is the most concerning name: revenue fell 9.8% YoY to $14.3B while net income collapsed 29.8%, compressing margins to 14.1% against $31.7B of debt—classic operating deleverage. XOM is similarly uninspiring with flat revenue and a 6.2% decline in net income, leaving margins at just 9.3%. I would need to see CAT's revenue stabilize and XOM's net margin recover above 11% before reconsidering either name.

views.note: Best margin-leverage combo in the universe: 38.3% net margin, +46% YoY net income growth, and only $14.8B total debt.
13.3% revenue growth with 36.9% net margins and 17.7% net income growth demonstrate durable cloud-driven earnings power.
Net income surged 64.2% YoY to $17.1B with margin expanding to 11.0%, though $58.8B debt and still-thin margins warrant monitoring.
56.2% net margin and 78% revenue growth are extraordinary, but the most recent data is from January and I need the April quarter to confirm sustainability.
Modest 5.1% revenue growth and 4.8% net income growth against $92.2B of total debt suggest limited upside from current fundamentals.
Solid 32.3% net margin and 9.1% earnings growth, but bank-specific leverage ($407B debt) makes the risk profile different from tech peers.
Revenue declined 2.1% YoY to $19.8B with essentially flat net income; defensive but no earnings growth catalyst visible.
Revenue grew 9.8% to $109.6B but 5.7% net margin is thin and YoY net income comparison is unavailable, limiting visibility.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% YoY signals severe operating deleverage; I need revenue to stabilize before reconsidering.
Flat revenue and a 6.2% decline in net income with only 9.3% net margin point to commodity-driven earnings compression.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Cooling Inflation and Softening Labor Market — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the macro regime as a prolonged pause with an easing bias: the Fed has held the upper bound at 4.50% for three months while the 12-month rate of change is -100 bp, CPI is running at just 2.3% YoY, and unemployment has drifted up 30 bp over the past year to 4.2%. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+86 bp YoY to +0.49 pp), consistent with the market pricing eventual cuts and a normalization of the curve. This backdrop is constructive for duration-sensitive growth equities and modestly positive for banks via NIM expansion, but the rising unemployment trend and still-restrictive policy rate argue against overweighting pure cyclicals. A CPI print re-accelerating above 3% or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would force me to revisit this call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth benefits from a steepening curve and easing bias with benign 2.3% inflation.
Similar duration tailwind as MSFT; moderating inflation and stable-to-lower long rates support multiples.
High-duration growth name that should re-rate if the Fed moves toward cuts, though elevated policy rate keeps some risk premium.
Curve steepening (+86 bp YoY in 10y-2y) supports NIM, but rising unemployment at 4.2% raises credit-loss concerns.
Late-cycle cyclical faces headwinds from softening labor market and still-restrictive 4.50% policy rate.
Defensive staple offers ballast if unemployment continues rising, but benign inflation reduces its pricing-power edge.
Energy is macro-neutral here; no strong inflation impulse to drive commodity upside, and softening demand signals from rising unemployment.
Consumer-facing growth with AWS duration exposure benefits from easing bias and controlled 2.3% YoY CPI.
Ad-driven revenue is cyclically sensitive but long-duration valuation benefits from curve steepening and stable 10y at 4.43%.
Defensive healthcare name is relatively rate-insensitive; macro setup neither strongly helps nor hurts.

memos.headline: MSFT Post-Earnings Momentum Stands Out; UNH Negative Narrative Deepening With Leadership Turnover
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. MSFT's +7.6% pop on its 4/30 results is the strongest positive reaction in the group and suggests the narrative around cloud/AI spending is being validated—sentiment momentum should persist near-term. UNH is the opposite story: a -22.4% earnings-day collapse on 4/17 followed by two separate officer departure 8-Ks (4/29 and 5/14) signals a compounding negative narrative that likely has not fully cleared. AAPL's -3.7% earnings reaction and a follow-on 'Other Events' 8-K on 5/12 suggest lingering unease, while GOOGL's +1.7% earnings reaction and steady flow of 'Other Events' filings point to a stable-to-positive tone. JPM's +4.0% earnings pop in mid-April was strong but is now over a month old, so I treat that positive impulse as largely priced.

views.note: Strongest post-earnings price reaction in the universe at +7.6% signals a positive narrative shift that likely has room to run.
A -22.4% earnings collapse compounded by two officer departure filings in the following weeks points to a deepening negative sentiment spiral.
The -3.7% earnings reaction and a subsequent Other Events filing suggest cautious tone; sentiment has not turned positive yet.
A +1.7% earnings pop and a steady cadence of routine 8-K filings suggest stable-to-positive sentiment without crowding.
The +4.0% earnings reaction was strong but occurred over a month ago; positive impulse is likely priced by now.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and officer changes create a mixed, low-conviction sentiment picture.
A -3.7% earnings drop mirrors consumer staples caution; subsequent filings have not shifted the negative tone.
Flat +0.4% earnings reaction and routine filings suggest no meaningful sentiment catalyst in either direction.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Doubles in Three Months While VIX Retreats — Structural Geopolitical Risk Remains Mispriced
memos.body: I see a dangerous divergence: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 469 has more than doubled over three months (+104.2%) and risen 26% in the past month alone, yet the VIX has collapsed 41% over the same month to 17.83. This tells me markets are pricing in a near-term détente (possibly the US-China tariff pause) while structural policy risk — export controls on advanced chips, energy security realignment, and supply-chain reshoring pressures — continues to build. WTI at $63.03 is down 11.3% over three months, consistent with demand-side fears from trade disruption rather than supply comfort. HY OAS at 3.20% has tightened 89bp in a month but remains 58bp wider than three months ago, suggesting credit markets still see residual risk. I have highest conviction on NVDA's geopolitical exposure given its April 8-K (likely related to export-control charges) and on CAT as a beneficiary of reshoring capex, and I remain cautious on names with heavy China manufacturing or revenue concentration.

views.note: The April 15 8-K likely reflects the H20 export-control write-down; further tightening of chip restrictions to China is a structural headwind that a single-quarter tariff pause does not resolve.

Apple's massive China assembly concentration is a persistent geopolitical risk, but the May 12 8-K and recent tariff pause provide short-term relief; I need clarity on any supply-chain diversification commitments before turning constructive.
Reshoring and infrastructure spending driven by policy uncertainty structurally benefit CAT's domestic order book; two recent 8-Ks suggest active investor communication around this theme.
WTI at $63 and down 11% in three months caps upside, but energy security policy could provide a floor; multiple 8-Ks suggest active capital-allocation updates but no clear geopolitical catalyst.
A steepening yield curve (+28bp over 3m) and elevated policy uncertainty typically boost bank trading revenue and NIM; JPM's three recent 8-Ks suggest proactive positioning.

Defensive positioning is tempting given elevated uncertainty, but PG's global supply chain faces tariff cost pass-through risk that three recent 8-Ks may be addressing; I lack detail to take a directional view.
